classification.difficultyReason: Two verifications by direct substitution and simplification. The cube-root part is a little less familiar, but everything is signposted.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Let $f(x)=4x-7$ and $g(x)=\dfrac{x+7}{4}$.

Show that $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions of each other by finding $f(g(x))$ and $g(f(x))$.

answer.short: $f(g(x))=x$ and $g(f(x))=x$ for all $x\in\mathbb R$. Hence $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=4\left(\frac{x+7}{4}\right)-7\\f(g(x))&=x+7-7\\f(g(x))&=x\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}g(f(x))&=\frac{(4x-7)+7}{4}\\g(f(x))&=\frac{4x}{4}\\g(f(x))&=x\end{align*}$$

Both compositions equal $x$ for every real $x$, so $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Let $f(x)=x^3-6$ and $g(x)=\sqrt[3]{x+6}$.

Show that $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions of each other by finding $f(g(x))$ and $g(f(x))$.

answer.short: $f(g(x))=x$ and $g(f(x))=x$ for all $x\in\mathbb R$. Hence $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=\left(\sqrt[3]{x+6}\right)^3-6\\f(g(x))&=x+6-6\\f(g(x))&=x\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}g(f(x))&=\sqrt[3]{(x^3-6)+6}\\g(f(x))&=\sqrt[3]{x^3}\\g(f(x))&=x\end{align*}$$

Both compositions equal $x$ for every real $x$, so $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions.
